question: Stage A1 section 1 defines concept reach as the share of a room's concepts that carry a theme_id. In this store every one of the 115388 concepts has a theme_id and sits in its theme's code_ids, so the share is 1.0 in all 705 rooms and no room size makes it fall. Did you mean another measure, for example concepts per second-order theme, or the share of concepts a theme's note or label actually describes? The threshold decides where cite.py must reach concepts at C2 to D3.
assumption: I declare concept_reach_threshold as 0 items: the measure gives no cut, and second-order themes grow at slope 0.23 on items against 0.53 for concepts, so every room is read at concept level from C2 to D3. I will revise it if your answer names another measure.

question: packets.py B2 builds one packet per round under the 50 KB ceiling, and stage B2 asks for 40 to 60 items including the ten biggest bags of notes-B1.md. Those ten hold about 3,500 concepts; leagueoflegends t02 alone renders 86,762 bytes, over the whole ceiling, and sweden t01 43,314. Even the median item renders 1,470 bytes. Should the B2 round be served in parts to the same reader (as B3 serves a large room), or is a size-capped hard set acceptable?

The ten biggest stay for stage B3 to flag. The bias toward smaller items is declared in notes-B2.md.

question: mem.py gates finds 202 one-way discriminators and 40 must_not_show lines with no discriminator on scheme.jsonl, and the freeze refuses them. At B2 every scheme change is a scheme_edits.jsonl line whose caused_by must name items of the hard or gold set, and most of these pairs touch no item. How should the repairs that no item caused be recorded: as scheme_edits lines with another caused_by (for example the gates check itself), or through mem.py gate as at B1?
assumption: At B2b-r1 I repair only the defects in pairs that round 1's edited themes belong to, each as a scheme_edits line caused by the round-1 items that divided readers on that theme. A one-way discriminator is mirrored by copying its question into the other gate, since each question names both sides. The rest wait for your answer and are repaired before the freeze.

question: Round 2 serves the hard set in parts to one reader (QB2-001), and the reader answers once per item after the last part. Some single items (leagueoflegends t02, 86,762 bytes) are larger than a part, so my splitter cuts inside an item's concepts. What MANIFEST.json form does fleet.py expect for such a group: on each part the B3 rule {group, part, parts} with items counted only on the last part (0 on earlier parts, whose reply is the end marker alone), or another form?
assumption: I write round 2 as P03-r2-p1 ... P03-r2-pN in out/_packets-B2/round-2/, each under 50 KB, with MANIFEST entries carrying count_key position, group P03-r2, part k, parts N, and items 0 on every part but the last, which carries all 50. Parts 1 to N-1 tell the reader to read on and reply with the end marker alone; the last part asks for every item's line, then the marker.
